text:
The Mammoth are winless in six (0-3-3), and Monday's 3-2 loss to Vancouver, with 5.96 expected goals to the Canucks' 3.03, was the whole season in one game. Utah sits at 10-9-3 with 23 points, and the record undersells the team.

Over 22 games André Tourigny's group has 54.67% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 58% at 5v5, numbers that belong to a contender. The problem is in its own net. Utah has allowed 10.88 more goals than its chances deserved. Sebastian Cossa has an .869 save percentage and is 4.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and Karel Vejmelka has drawn the "he has a job to do" treatment from KSL Sports after the San Jose loss. By our count that adds up to about 4.4 fewer points than its play has earned.

The injuries haven't helped. Dylan Guenther is out two to four weeks with an upper-body injury, and Nick Schmaltz has a lower-body injury. Logan Cooley came back Monday, with 14 points in his last ten. The line of Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton has controlled 75% of the expected goals in its minutes, while the top pair of MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev has been outscored 13-6 despite winning the chances.

Our numbers still give Utah a 64% playoff chance, projecting about 94 points. What to watch is simple: whether anyone in the crease gives this team league-average goaltending.
headline: Good team, bad goaltending, six without a win
